title: Juniper and Pearl's Singing Pearl
markdown:
Juniper was a seal pup. She had the wiggliest nose in the whole ocean. When she was excited, her nose wiggled so much, it looked like it was trying to do a little dance all by itself. Her bark sounded like a happy squeak: “Arf-arf-arf.” She loved to zoom through the water, making bubbly splashes, and play hide-and-seek with the happy waves. And her very, very best friend was Pearl.

Pearl wasn’t a seal pup at all. She was a tide sprite. She looked like a teeny-tiny fairy, but instead of fluttery wings, she had sparkly water droplets that twinkled all around her like a little crown. Her hair was the colour of the prettiest seaweed, all soft green and brown. She could zoom through the water like a tiny silver fish, leaving a trail of glittery bubbles behind her. Her laugh sounded like tiny bells tinkling: “Ting-a-ling-ling.” Pearl knew everything about the sea. She knew where the shyest little hermit crabs hid their funny shells, and which squishy anemones tickled your flippers the most.

One sunny morning, when the sea was sparkly like a million dropped diamonds, Pearl zipped up to Juniper, who was snoozing on a warm rock. Juniper’s nose twitched a little, probably dreaming of tasty fish. “Juniper. Juniper,” Pearl chimed, her voice like a happy little ripple. “Guess what I found out? Guess, guess, guess?”

Juniper opened one sleepy dark eye. “Arf?” she asked, her nose already starting to wiggle-dance, because it knew Pearl meant an adventure.

“There’s a special pearl,” Pearl whispered, her voice full of bubbly excitement. “It’s hidden in the rock pools near the whispering caves, and it only opens when you sing the sea its own reflection. Singing to the sea. Can you even imagine?” Pearl giggled again, doing a little twirl.

Juniper sat up with a plop, shaking sea spray from her smooth fur. A secret pearl? That sounded like the best adventure ever. Her nose wiggled so fast, it was a blur. “A pearl? For us? Just for us to find?” she barked, doing a happy wiggle-dance.

“Come on,” Pearl giggled, doing a little loop-de-loop. “We have to find it before the tide goes out too far.”

So off they went. Juniper padded along the wet sand, making little swishy sounds, and Pearl shimmered beside her. They peeked into the rock pools. There were pools that looked like big shallow puddles, perfect for a little seal pup splash. And there were pools that were deep, with tiny silver fish darting about like speedy raindrops.

First they found a pool where little pink shrimps were playing tag. “Is it this one?” Juniper asked, nudging it with her wet nose. “Nope,” said Pearl, shaking her bubbly head. “Too busy playing tag.”

Next they found a pool, all green and mossy. A grumpy-looking starfish was taking a nap on a rock. “This one? Is the pearl hiding under the starfish?” Juniper nudged again. “Too sleepy,” muttered the starfish, without opening an eye, and Pearl shook her bubbly head. “We need a pool that’s awake and ready to play.”

Then they looked under wavy seaweed that tickled Juniper’s whiskers, and past sea anemones that swayed like colourful dancers. Juniper’s nose wiggled faster and faster. A hermit crab peeked from a spiral shell and said, “Not here, not here,” before scuttling sideways into a shadow.

At last they saw it. Tucked away in a little crevice, almost hidden by a piece of smooth driftwood, was a pearl. It wasn’t big, but it shone with a soft light. It was shut tight, like it was fast asleep. “This must be it,” Juniper barked, her whole body wiggling.

Pearl zoomed closer. “It’s so beautiful. But how do we make it open?” She remembered her words. “Sing the sea its own reflection.”

“Sing the sea?” Juniper tilted her head. “How do you sing a reflection? Does the sea have ears?” She let out a little chuckle.

Pearl giggled, that tinkling sound again. “No, silly. The reflection. Look.” She pointed to the surface of the rock pool. The bright blue sky, the fluffy white clouds, and Juniper’s own excited wiggling face were all mirrored there, like a wobbly picture.

“You have to sing that,” Pearl explained. “Sing to the wobbly picture of the sky and your happy face in the water.”

Juniper took a deep breath. This was a very funny idea. Singing to a reflection. But Pearl was the expert. So Juniper looked at the sky in the water, and she started to hum. It wasn’t a loud bark, but a gentle happy hum. “Huuuuuummm. Arf-arf-hummmm,” she sang, her voice soft and sweet.

And Pearl joined in. “Ting-a-ling. Hummm. Shimmer, shimmer, clouds drift by.” Her little voice was like tiny wind chimes. They sang together, looking at the watery sky and their happy reflected faces.

The pearl began to shine brighter and brighter. Flicker, flicker, gleam. Then, with a soft happy pop, like a bubble bursting, it opened. Inside, it was filled with the most beautiful tiny swirling colours — soft blues and greens and purples, like a miniature rainbow dancing. And from inside, a soft sweet scent like sea salt and warm sunshine wafted out, making Juniper’s nose wiggle with delight.

Juniper nudged Pearl gently with her nose. “We did it,” she barked happily.

Pearl giggled, landing on Juniper’s head for a quick happy hug. “We sang to the sea, and the sea sang back with the pearl.”

Kindness sung to the water opens what hurry cannot. And their tale is still told when tide sprites tinkle over the rock pools. The sun shone down, warming them, and Juniper and Pearl splashed in the sparkling sea, the open pearl still humming its little rainbow in the crevice, and the waves playing hide-and-seek around their flippers.
characters: Juniper (a seal pup), Pearl (a tide sprite)
author: StoryGen Community
